title: Sensex Surges 905 Points, Nifty Tops 22,900 as Banking and FMCG Stocks Lead
excerpt: The Sensex closed at 74,151.04 and the Nifty at 22,936.75 on Thursday, snapping a two-day losing streak as a US Fed rate hold, easing crude and Adani Ports' strong results lifted sentiment.
body:
• The BSE Sensex jumped 905.01 points, or 1.24%, to close at 74,151.04 on Thursday, while the NSE Nifty rose 237.90 points, or 1.05%, to 22,936.75.
  • Realty (+2.75%), FMCG (+2.34%) and PSU Bank (+2.20%) led the sector table; auto was the only major laggard, slipping 0.24%.
  • Adani Ports was the top Sensex gainer, rising over 5% after reporting an 18% increase in quarterly net profit to Rs 3,682.44 crore.
  • For investors: the Nifty has reclaimed its 20-day moving average, with 23,000 the immediate hurdle and 22,800 the support analysts are watching.

Indian equity benchmarks staged their strongest single-day rally in weeks on Thursday, with the Sensex soaring 905 points on heavy buying in banking and FMCG shares and a fall in crude oil prices. The rally snapped a two-day losing streak and came a day after the US Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged at 3.75%-4%.

The 30-share BSE Sensex opened at 73,268.47, touched a high of 74,166.16 and closed near the day's peak at 74,151.04. The Nifty climbed from an intraday low of 22,656.75 to settle at 22,936.75, within touching distance of the 23,000 mark, according to The Hindu BusinessLine's market coverage.

What drove the rally

Three forces combined. The Fed's decision to hold rates steady calmed global markets. Crude oil eased after spiking above $115 a barrel earlier in the week, relieving pressure on India's import bill. And institutional money returned: foreign portfolio investors were net buyers of Indian equities for a second straight session on Wednesday, purchasing shares worth Rs 872 crore, according to provisional exchange data cited in market reports.

Adani Ports emerged as the biggest gainer, rising over 5% after the company reported an 18% increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 3,682.44 crore for the September quarter, driven by higher revenue. Kotak Mahindra Bank, Power Grid, Eternal, Bajaj Finance, State Bank of India, Hindustan Unilever, Titan, NTPC, Bharat Electronics and Infosys also closed higher. Trent, Maruti Suzuki, Tech Mahindra and HDFC Bank were among the laggards.

Breadth beyond the benchmarks

The gains were broad-based. The Nifty Midcap 100 climbed 0.99% to 57,841.65 and the Nifty Smallcap 100 advanced 0.95% to 18,811.35, a sign the recovery extended beyond large caps. The India VIX, the market's fear gauge, fell about 6% to around 15.14, signalling easing near-term nervousness. The rupee traded marginally stronger at about 95.25 to the dollar.

"Buying was visible across several pockets, with realty, FMCG and select banking stocks leading the recovery."

— Ajit Mishra, SVP Research, Religare Broking

What to watch next

Analysts say the Nifty has strongly reclaimed its 20-day moving average with a consolidation breakout on the daily chart. The 23,000 level remains an immediate hurdle; above it, traders see the previous swing high of 23,175. As long as the index holds above the 22,800 support zone, the short-term outlook stays positive — but the September-quarter earnings calendar and crude's direction will decide whether Thursday's rally becomes a durable recovery.
